title: Complex Eigenvalues of a Real Matrix
quickIdea: A real matrix has non-real eigenvalues only in conjugate pairs, so an odd-order real matrix always has at least one real eigenvalue and the pair multiplies to a positive real number.
remember: If a + bi is an eigenvalue of a real matrix then a - bi is too, with the same algebraic multiplicity.
The pair multiplies to a^2 + b^2, which is positive, so a conjugate pair contributes a positive factor to the determinant.
A real 2x2 has complex eigenvalues exactly when (tr A)^2 < 4 det A.
A real matrix with a non-real eigenvalue has no real eigenvector for it; the eigenvector is complex.
The rotation [[0,-1],[1,0]] is the model case: eigenvalues i and -i, trace 0 and determinant 1.

example.prompt: Two eigenvalues of a real 3x3 matrix P are 2 + sqrt(-1) and 3. Find det P.
example.work: A real matrix has real coefficients in its characteristic polynomial, so a non-real root forces its conjugate to be a root as well. The third eigenvalue is therefore 2 - sqrt(-1). The determinant is the product: (2+i)(2-i) x 3 = (4+1) x 3 = 15.
example.answer: det P = 15, which is GATE CSE 2016 Set 1 Q.5.

gateAngle: 2016 Set 1 Q.5 is the whole pattern: an odd-order real matrix, one non-real eigenvalue given, the conjugate inferred, the determinant taken as the product. The distractors come from multiplying only the two given eigenvalues, or from treating the missing eigenvalue as free.

variations.label: ORIGINAL PYQ-STYLE QUESTION
variations.question: A real 2x2 matrix has trace 4 and determinant 13. Are its eigenvalues real?
variations.why: The discriminant is (tr)^2 - 4 det = 16 - 52 = -36 < 0, so the quadratic lambda^2 - 4 lambda + 13 has a conjugate complex pair with real part tr/2 = 2.

variations.label: CONCEPTUAL PRACTICE QUESTION
variations.question: Why can a real matrix never have exactly one non-real eigenvalue?
variations.answer: Its characteristic polynomial has real coefficients, and a real polynomial's non-real roots occur in conjugate pairs because conjugation fixes the coefficients.
variations.why: This is why the count of non-real eigenvalues of a real matrix is always even, and why an odd-order real matrix must have a real eigenvalue.

variations.label: PREDICTED VARIATION
variations.question: A real 4x4 matrix has eigenvalues 1, 3 and 2 + i among its four. What is the fourth, and what is det A?
variations.answer: The fourth is 2 - i, and det A = 1 x 3 x (2+i)(2-i) = 15.
variations.why: The conjugate fills the missing slot, and the determinant is the product of all four, with the pair contributing 5.

trap.what: Treating the eigenvalue that was not listed as free, or forgetting that the determinant is the product over all n eigenvalues including the conjugate.
trap.why: A real matrix has a fixed multiset of n eigenvalues counted with multiplicity; a non-real one pins down its partner, so the set is complete once one of the pair is known.
trap.counterexample: For a real 3x3 with 2+i and 3 given, taking det = (2+i) x 3 = 6 + 3i is impossible for a real matrix, and the true value is 15.

check.question: A real 2x2 matrix has determinant 1 and trace 0. What are its eigenvalues?
check.explanation: lambda^2 + 1 = 0. The matrix is a rotation by 90 degrees, which turns every real vector, so it has no real eigenvector at all.
